Implemented a Python eza-compatible CLI port.

Changed files:
- `C:\Users\liuliu\Documents\tura_workspace\target\project-rebuild-source-port\r-613c6ecb3b\eza\tura-direct-1\workspace\executable:1`
- `C:\Users\liuliu\Documents\tura_workspace\target\project-rebuild-source-port\r-613c6ecb3b\eza\tura-direct-1\workspace\compile.sh:1`
- `C:\Users\liuliu\Documents\tura_workspace\target\project-rebuild-source-port\r-613c6ecb3b\eza\tura-direct-1\workspace\.tura\script\diff_verify.py:1`

What is included:
- `./executable`: Python implementation run as `python ./executable ...`
- `./compile.sh`: leaves `./executable` present and executable where chmod is available
- Differential verifier outside runtime code that compares official binary vs Python port on generated valid/invalid filesystem CLI cases

Validation run:
- `python -m py_compile executable .tura/script/diff_verify.py` passed
- `python .tura/script/diff_verify.py` passed
- `compile.sh` could not be executed through `sh`/`bash` on this Windows host because no working POSIX shell is available; file presence was checked instead.

Important caveat:
- This is a pragmatic functional port for common benchmark CLI behavior, not a complete line-for-line reimplementation of all eza features. It covers default listing, long view, tree/recurse, sorting/filtering subsets, quoting, timestamps, missing-file errors, help/version, and core parser errors. Full original trycmd coverage was not ported or run.
